component.name: deepmap
component.description: Per-project Neo4j code knowledge graph + intent-summary embeddings + 3-arm Weighted-RRF hybrid search for Claude Code

properties.name: deepmap:sbom_status
properties.value: SEED (hand-maintained) — neo4j, mcp and graphifyy carry their VALIDATED version RANGES, identical to requirements.txt, both installers and CI (tests/compliance_gates.py fails on any drift); anyio carries the floor requirements.txt declares for it (mcp's own; both installers install it next to mcp with that floor, CI gets it through mcp); the other pip components stay unpinned (no known breaking release). A range is not a resolved release: regenerate this SBOM from the installed environment in the build for an exact-version bill

properties.name: deepmap:apoc_not_used
properties.value: APOC (Core, Apache-2.0) is NOT used: DeepMap neither fetches, enables nor calls it. The Neo4j distribution carries a disabled labs/apoc-*-core.jar; DeepMap leaves it disabled.

properties.name: deepmap:ranx_not_a_dependency
properties.value: ranx (MIT) is not a dependency and is not shipped: fusion is the pure-Python _weighted_rrf in build/retrieval.py, nothing imports ranx, and requirements.txt and the installers exclude it.

properties.name: deepmap:mcp_neo4j_cypher_not_shipped
properties.value: mcp-neo4j-cypher (neo4j-contrib/mcp-neo4j, MIT) is not a dependency and is not shipped: DeepMap's read-only Cypher tool (deepmap_cypher) is its own code. Neo4j's official MCP server (neo4j/mcp, GPL-3.0) is likewise not shipped.

components.name: Neo4j Community Edition
components.version: 5.26.32 (the provisioner's default NEO4J_VERSION for a new store, validated end to end; a store created with 5.26.0 keeps it until setup or `provision.py neo4j-upgrade` moves it; the NEO4J_VERSION env var overrides both)

properties.name: deepmap:distribution
properties.value: prerequisite — fetched from the official source (dist.neo4j.org) at setup; NOT bundled or redistributed; its code is not modified (setup writes only DeepMap's own settings into neo4j.conf on the user's machine, including dbms.usage_report.enabled=false); accessed arms-length over Bolt

properties.name: deepmap:compatibility
properties.value: Only copyleft component; fetch-not-bundle + arms-length Bolt keeps DeepMap's MIT code free of the GPLv3 combined-work obligation

properties.name: deepmap:install
properties.value: pip install --upgrade "graphifyy>=0.8.39,<0.8.52"

properties.name: deepmap:distribution
properties.value: SHIPPED — the multi-language extraction engine (DEEPMAP_EXTRACTOR=graphify|auto). Installed BARE (no extras) by both installers + requirements.txt with `pip install --upgrade "graphifyy>=0.8.39,<0.8.52"` — the --upgrade lifts an older in-range copy to the top of the range. NEVER graphifyy[all] — the optional LLM SDK extras (openai/anthropic/bedrock) are deliberately excluded so a default install ships NO LLM SDK. Validated at 0.8.39 and 0.8.51 (the releases between were diffed statically); 0.8.52+ and 0.9.x are outside the validated range (build/graphify_extract.py SUPPORTED_GRAPHIFY_SPEC).

properties.name: deepmap:note
properties.value: Upstream AST engine (Graphify-Labs/graphify, formerly safishamsi/graphify), used unchanged. MIT for every release the pin allows; upstream relicensed to Apache-2.0 from 0.9.25 (2026-07-22), so re-check the licence before widening the pin. PyPI package is `graphifyy`; the import name `graphify` is used unchanged. MIT attribution retained. DeepMap invokes only `graphify update --no-cluster` (NO LLM, NO clustering, NO network) — multi-language extraction is zero-egress by construction. Base wheel pulls ~25 tree-sitter grammars.

properties.name: deepmap:distribution
properties.value: bundled (pip); Python Bolt driver, installed with `pip install --upgrade "neo4j>=6.0.1,<7"`. Floor: 6.0.1 is the lowest release the full gate suite passed on — 5.x drivers failed it when measured (no neo4j.exceptions.ConnectionPoolError, which the CLI's error classifier needed until it was made defensive; 5.6 and older also reject notifications_min_severity) and are not re-validated, and 6.0.0 cannot import its bolt layer on Windows; ceiling: 7 is unreleased.

properties.name: deepmap:install
properties.value: pip install --upgrade "mcp>=1.24,<2"

properties.name: deepmap:distribution
properties.value: bundled (pip); the MCP Python SDK — both MCP servers `from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP` at module load. Installed with `pip install --upgrade "mcp>=1.24,<2"`. Floor: 1.13 and older die at import next to current pydantic, and 1.14-1.23 lack the streamable-HTTP client the MCP gates drive; ceiling: 2.x removed mcp.server.fastmcp.

properties.name: deepmap:declared
properties.value: anyio>=4.5 in requirements.txt — mcp's own floor (mcp 1.28.1 metadata: anyio>=4.5), so declaring it never changes what pip resolves next to mcp; no ceiling (no known breaking release)

properties.name: deepmap:distribution
properties.value: bundled (pip); both installers install it next to mcp, with requirements.txt's floor, in mcp's own pip command; CI gets it through mcp. Imported directly: the MCP servers run each tool body in a worker thread under a deadline (build/mcp_bounds.py) and bound the search server's project-guard roots request (build/deepmap_search_server.py), so requirements.txt declares it rather than leaving it to a transitive dependency.
